open_points.subject: current persistence baseline for renewed grants and assignments
open_points.text: Where the former text and the accepted spec disagree, the accepted spec is kept
open_points.question: Does the 2026-11-22 decision replace the accepted Factory schema for ProjectViewerGrant, StaffProjectAssignment and ProducerProjectGrant, or must the old one-record-per-pair schema still be kept?
options: The 2026-11-22 decision supersedes the accepted schema for all three tables.
The accepted one-record-per-pair schema remains authoritative.
Only some of the three tables adopt the new history model.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the later owner decision as superseding the accepted schema for all three tables.

witness.initial: A viewer-project pair has one revoked grant stored under the accepted schema and no active grant.
events: An administrator calls grant_viewer_project for the same viewer-project pair after the 2026-11-22 change.
outcomes: Keeping the accepted schema's pair-wide UNIQUE constraint makes the insert fail and access cannot be restored.
Applying the later rule permits a new grant row because only active rows must be unique.
witness.observer: The administrator sees either a failed grant operation or restored access.

open_points.subject: A8 ownership of active grant uniqueness
open_points.question: Which modules own and consume A8's INV-009 after uniqueness means one active ProjectViewerGrant or ProducerProjectGrant per pair? The mapped owner and consumers neither manage those grants nor implement their persistence.
options: Move grant uniqueness out of A8 and assign it to viewer_access/service_identity and their repositories.
Keep it in A8 but add the grant services and repositories as consumers and name a suitable primary owner.
Split A8 so snapshot/photo/payment idempotency and grant uniqueness have separate owners.
open_points.default_guess: Split grant uniqueness from A8 and assign each grant lifecycle to its application service, with its repository responsible only for atomic SQLite enforcement.

open_points.subject: partial-unique-index and history responsibility
open_points.text: the table and column layout is the persistence closure's.
open_points.question: For each of ProjectViewerGrant, StaffProjectAssignment and ProducerProjectGrant, which owner decides the one-active-row invariant, which owner defines active-only pair reads and retained history, and which module implements the partial unique index? State 3 also says application modules own the grants or assignments, repositories hide SQL, and viewer_access_repository owns grant uniqueness.
options: The application service owns lifecycle and query semantics; the persistence closure owns the index definition; the repository implements both.
Each repository owns the invariant and active/history query semantics.
The persistence closure owns all three concerns and application services merely call its ports.
open_points.default_guess: Make the application service own lifecycle and active-only behavior, the persistence closure own the partial-index schema, and the repository own atomic enforcement without owning the product decision.

open_points.subject: upgrade from pair-wide uniqueness to partial uniqueness
open_points.text: One active grant per pair is now kept by a partial unique index (SPEC_STANDARD §6.3, tenth addition); the revoked records stay as history.
open_points.question: How must an existing database remove the old pair-wide UNIQUE constraint, install the partial unique index, preserve revoked rows, and advance its schema revision for all three affected tables?
options: Provide an in-place transactional migration that rebuilds each affected SQLite table and advances the schema revision.
Support only fresh databases and explicitly declare existing databases incompatible.
Keep the old constraint on existing databases, so re-granting works only on newly created deployments.
open_points.default_guess: Add a transactional, revisioned SQLite migration that rebuilds all three affected tables, preserves their rows, removes pair-wide uniqueness and creates the partial unique indexes.

witness.initial: A deployed database was created by the accepted Factory schema and contains a revoked row for each of the affected pair types.
events: The deployment is upgraded to code generated from the new design.
An administrator grants or assigns one of those pairs again.
outcomes: A schema migration removes the old constraint and the new active row is inserted successfully.
Only the new partial index is added; the old table-level UNIQUE constraint remains and rejects the insert.
witness.observer: The administrator and the newly granted principal see whether access can be restored.
